# Aarhus Universitetshospital, Psykiatrien

Aarhus Universitetshospital, Psykiatrien is a psychiatric hospital division that plays a formal governance role in Denmark's national **ADHD-databasen** (ADHD database), a clinical quality register that tracks ADHD diagnosis and treatment across Danish child, adolescent, and adult psychiatry. The institution is named as one of the bodies represented in the database's chairmanship (formandskab), which is otherwise made up of senior consultants (overlæger) from the hospital and from DPS Midtjylland [^src1].

Within Aarhus Universitetshospital, Psykiatrien, the corpus identifies two specific clinical units engaged in ADHD work: the Børne- og Ungdomspsykiatrisk Afdeling (BUA), the child and adolescent psychiatry department, and a "Team for ADHD" housed in Klinik 2, afdeling for psykoser (the psychosis department) [^src1]. The hospital appears again as a named contributor in the ADHD database's 2024 annual report [^src2], and later in the report's appendices it is identified more precisely as part of Region Midtjylland: "Aarhus Universitetshospital, Psykiatrien, Region Midtjylland" [^src3].

These mentions sit within a larger documented story: the ADHD-databasen's annual reports, produced by Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) and later by Sundhedsvæsenets Kvalitetsinstitut, track deteriorating conditions in Danish child and adolescent psychiatry — rising referral numbers, longer waiting times, and falling performance on most quality indicators [^src1]. The 2024 report, led by Shelagh Powell and Simon Hjerrild, for the first time incorporated data from the adult population and private hospitals, alongside continued problems with registration practices, staffing, and waiting times, with Region Midt singled out for particular focus on improving registration practices and shortening assessment pathways [^src2]. Aarhus Universitetshospital, Psykiatrien, as a Region Midtjylland institution with representation in the database's chairmanship, is thus positioned as one of the clinical actors both reporting on and responsible for addressing these systemic quality challenges [^src1][^src2][^src3].

No relationships or discrete factual claims specific to this entity (beyond its named mentions) are recorded in the extracted data.
